description: Recovered advice-only response regressions: 11 cases and 60 concept assertions. Compare matched with_skill and baseline sessions using independent grading. Validate every concrete CLI command separately against versioned help evidence, as described in README.md.

evals.name: snapdragon-resnet-build
evals.prompt: i just got a snapdragon x elite dev box and i want to run microsoft/resnet-50 on the npu. can you walk me through getting it built and benchmarked? i want to see latency numbers at the end. give me actual commands i can copy paste.

assertions.text: Recommends inspecting the model before starting the build pipeline.
Identifies QNN as the target EP for Snapdragon X Elite and checks that it is available.
Does not substitute OpenVINO or VitisAI for the requested Qualcomm NPU. Any fallback is explicitly identified as not meeting the NPU target.
Explains a model-producing build path, using config plus build or the necessary primitive stages, before benchmarking the published artifact.
Includes a perf step that would measure latency, without fabricating a measured number in this advice-only response.
Every concrete command uses subcommands, flags, and argument shapes supported by the supplied or consulted CLI-help evidence; a generic check-help disclaimer does not excuse invalid commands.
Includes installation prerequisites or a clear pointer to them because this is a fresh dev box.

evals.name: ryzen-ai-quick-benchmark
evals.prompt: I have an AMD Ryzen AI laptop and I want to know the fastest way to see how fast facebook/convnext-tiny-224 runs on my NPU. I don't really care about the artifact, just the number.

assertions.text: Identifies VitisAI as the target AMD NPU provider, subject to actual device and EP availability.
Recommends perf against the source model as the primary benchmark action rather than requiring a separately saved model artifact.
Does not require manually executing export, optimize, quantize, and compile as separate steps before the benchmark.
Mentions inspecting the model first as a sanity check.
Every concrete command is supported by versioned CLI-help evidence; plausible-looking flags alone do not pass.
Includes installation prerequisites or a pointer because the prompt gives no signal of an existing winml installation.

evals.name: npu-vs-cpu-comparison
evals.prompt: i have a ViT model (google/vit-base-patch16-224) and im trying to decide whether to ship the NPU version or just use CPU. running on a snapdragon x elite. whats the cleanest way to get apples-to-apples latency numbers from both?

assertions.text: Recommends inspecting the model before building or benchmarking it.
Identifies QNN as the Snapdragon NPU target and verifies its availability.
Recommends one build workflow with published intermediate and compiled outputs, then benchmarks the appropriate outputs on NPU and CPU with comparable measurement settings.
Uses a published pre-compile ONNX artifact for the CPU benchmark rather than the QNN-compiled model or an assumed private cache file.
Explains that EP-compiled artifacts are tied to their target provider and cannot serve as the CPU comparison artifact.
All concrete commands and any intermediate-output options are supported by versioned CLI-help evidence.
Includes installation prerequisites or a pointer because prior winml installation is not established.

evals.name: is-model-supported
evals.prompt: Before I commit to building `nvidia/segformer-b1-finetuned-ade-512-512` end-to-end on my Intel NPU, is there a way to know if it's going to make it through the full pipeline? Burned half a day last time on a model that exported fine but then died at the optimize stage.

assertions.text: Starts with inspect as a cheap configuration-only check that does not download model weights.
Recommends analyze on an available exported ONNX after inspection, explaining that an export is needed if no ONNX exists yet.
Identifies OpenVINO as the Intel NPU target, subject to device and provider availability.
Explains the analyzer's supported/partial/unsupported operator checks for the target EP without promising that inspection or analysis guarantees full build success.
Does not answer only by asking the user to attempt the entire expensive build pipeline.

evals.name: optimize-failure-recovery
evals.prompt: i'm building microsoft/swin-large-patch4-window7-224 for QNN on snapdragon x elite. inspect and export went through fine but winml optimize keeps erroring with something about an unsupported op pattern. what do i do?

assertions.text: Recommends analyzing the already exported ONNX as an early diagnostic step.
Explains how target-EP operator analysis can help identify the problematic pattern without inventing a diagnosis not supported by the actual error.
Does not recommend hand-editing the ONNX graph as the normal recovery path.
Suggests a supported optimization/quantization configuration change or an explicit model/EP limitation, instead of an unsupported workaround.
Requests or inspects the actual error and relevant help before guessing the failing operator, provider, or stage.

evals.name: install-setup
evals.prompt: i just got my snapdragon x elite dev box and i don't have winml installed yet. python 3.10 is already on the system. give me the actual install commands i should run to get going before i can do anything else.

assertions.text: Recommends Python 3.11 and explains that the existing Python 3.10 does not satisfy the package's >=3.11,<3.12 requirement.
Creates an isolated Python 3.11 environment using uv or an equivalent explicit interpreter selection, rather than installing into system Python 3.10.
Installs the winml-cli package from PyPI into that environment, not a different generic winml package.
Includes a post-install CLI and/or provider-discovery verification step.

evals.name: local-onnx-file
evals.prompt: i already have a resnet50.onnx file on disk from a previous export — about 100MB. how do i get it benchmarked on my intel core ultra NPU without re-downloading anything from huggingface?

assertions.text: Identifies OpenVINO as the Intel Core Ultra NPU target, subject to actual availability.
Uses perf on the local ONNX as the benchmark entry point, passing its path through the supported model flag rather than an unsupported positional argument.
Does not re-export or re-download the source Hugging Face model when the local ONNX is already available.
Every concrete command uses flags and argument shapes supported by the evaluated CLI-help evidence.

evals.name: config-build-for-ci
evals.prompt: we want to add a CI job that rebuilds an optimized resnet50 (targeting qnn) every time the model config changes. i want one json config that lives in the repo and a reproducible build step. how should i set this up?

assertions.text: Recommends generating a config and invoking build from that config rather than maintaining a manually chained primitive pipeline.
Identifies the generated build configuration JSON as the version-controlled build input.
Does not claim config values override explicit CLI flags; if discussing precedence, correctly states CLI options override config defaults.

Addresses controlled model revisions, CLI/dependency versions, target hardware/EP availability, or cache/rebuild policy for repeatability; does not promise byte-identical artifacts from a config alone.
Includes installing winml-cli in a compatible environment on the fresh CI runner before invoking the build.

evals.name: seq2seq-out-of-scope
evals.prompt: i want to deploy salesforce/codet5p-220m on my snapdragon x elite NPU for offline code summarization in a VSCode extension. the model takes a code snippet and outputs a natural-language summary. walk me through the winml pipeline?

assertions.text: Identifies the generative seq2seq architecture and applies the skill's general scope rule, not a checkpoint-name blacklist.
Clearly states that the request is outside this skill's declared scope without incorrectly claiming that all current CLI generative paths are unsupported.
Does not prescribe this skill's classic-model export/optimize/quantize/compile/build/perf pipeline for the generative model.
Points to current model/runtime documentation or an appropriate generative workflow; does not promise unverified model support or repeat an expired roadmap as current fact.

evals.name: ambiguous-run-intent
evals.prompt: i want to run resnet-50 on my snapdragon x elite. how do i do that with winml?

assertions.text: Acknowledges the distinction between measuring latency and producing a deployable artifact, by clarifying intent or presenting both paths with a reasoned recommendation.
Does not prescribe perf, then build, then perf again as the normal workflow.
If prescribing both model building and benchmarking, publishes the model through build before running perf on that artifact.
Recommends inspecting the model before starting the pipeline.
Identifies QNN as the Snapdragon NPU target and checks availability.
All concrete commands are supported by versioned CLI-help evidence, not inferred from plausible naming.
Includes installation prerequisites because the prompt does not establish a working installation.

evals.name: perf-output-recovery
evals.prompt: i already ran `winml perf -m microsoft/resnet-50 --device npu` on my snapdragon x elite and got latency numbers back. now i want to take that optimized onnx and ship it with my app. where did winml perf put the model file?

assertions.text: Explains that perf's published output is benchmark metrics JSON, not the deployable model.
Treats perf's internal build/cache artifacts as opaque rather than a supported deployment output.
Recommends build with an explicit supported output location to publish the deployable model.
Explains that the build configuration should first be generated or supplied.
Does not invent a cache path or a hidden perf flag that supposedly publishes the model.
All concrete commands and output flags are supported by the evaluated CLI-help evidence.
